exposure: fetal heart rate monitoring method (Doppler vs. Pinard stethoscope)
outcome: abnormal fetal heart rate (<120 or >160 bpm)
perinatal outcomes (fresh stillbirths, 24-hour neonatal admissions, and deaths)
cohort: 2,844 women with gestational age >=37 weeks, cephalic presentation, normal FHR on admission, and cervical dilatation <7 cm
finding: Intermittent FHR monitoring using Doppler was associated with an increased detection of abnormal FHR compared to Pinard.
mod_finding: The incidence of cesarean delivery was similar between the Doppler and Pinard groups (12.0% vs. 12.2%).
followup_time: 24 hours after birth (for neonatal admissions and deaths)
